title: The video with a hole at minute nine
blurb: Segments were marked done before encoding and corrupt input retried forever.
prompt: A finished video glitched at minute nine, because the draft marked a segment done before its encode returned and the crashed worker was never retried, while a corrupt segment elsewhere looped the job for hours. Review it, fix it, and prove completion follows encoding and failures classify.
aiNote: The draft marks segments complete when they are claimed rather than when the encode returns, so a worker crash leaves a hole that the manifest still reports as full, and it retries corrupt input indefinitely instead of classifying it as terminal.
testIdea: Kill a worker mid-segment and assert the segment is re-encoded and the manifest is gapless; corrupt one input segment and assert the job fails with that index after bounded attempts; replay a submit and assert one job.
followUps: How do you bound retries when input corruption is intermittent?
When should transcoding prefer quality over speed?
